articles.title: GTA 6's First Official Preview Reveals 5 Juicy New Details
articles.subtitle: GTA 6 evolves many of Red Dead Redemption 2's stellar mechanics As Grand Theft Auto 6 leakers threaten to spoil the game, Rockstar is stepping in to give fans a more polished look at it ahead of Netflix's trailer reveal.
articles.author: Polygon
articles.content:
GTA 6 evolves many of Red Dead Redemption 2's stellar mechanics

As Grand Theft Auto 6 leakers threaten to spoil the game, Rockstar is stepping in to give fans a more polished look at it ahead of Netflix's trailer reveal. Dazed magazine's September issue features the first and only preview of the game this year. There's a lot to dig into in the mag's write-up, which includes never-before-seen pictures of the open-world game as well as exclusive interviews with Rockstar's developers.

Though the preview is worth reading in full, here are some of the highlights.

GTA 6 will be Rockstar's most realistic game ever

GTA 6 is doubling down on many of Red Dead Redemption 2 's more grounded mechanics, Dazed reports. Screenshots already alluded to the possibility that Jason and Lucia's appearance will be impacted by what you do, but the preview shares specific details. Aspects like eating and physical exertion can impact the protagonists' appearance, as can your general play style.

If you don't sleep, for example, that will be visible on Jason and Lucia's faces. The realism will be present in smaller details as well, like the ability to purchase phone cases and headphones. Cars should handle better now too, thanks to designers who are also professional race car drivers.

NPCs are getting a major upgrade in GTA 6

Unsurprisingly, Rockstar's approach to GTA 6 was a perfectionist one. The studio dedicated an entire team to NPC behavior, and the contributions of these developers were highly specific. One designer, for example, helped develop a "fashion ecosystem" for the NPCs that reflects their "taste, lifestyle, and affluence.

" As the recent beach leak proved, GTA 6 will feature the widest variety of NPCs in a Rockstar game to date — and those NPCs will be tailored to their regions. Districts have always felt distinct in GTA games, but Rockstar took things one step further by hiring 50 artists to design the murals around town.

Developers spent time with everyone from ex-criminals to club promoters to learn how to best bring characters and NPCs to life. NPCs are programmed to react realistically to how Jason and Lucia behave and what they look like. The aim was to create an environment of "total immersion." In practice, this means that players shouldn't expect to be able to mow through the game like a murderous tyrant. Perhaps the Wanted system won't bring back tank chases after all?

Jason and Lucia's gameplay will be fluid

While players are free to approach the game without their romantic counterpart, sticking together will allow for some unique scenarios. Players can task one character with driving and the other with shooting — and then seamlessly switch between the two at a moment's notice. Fans could also make one character the navigator while the other scrolls the in-game social media to pass the time.

Actions have consequences

Dazed did not get into specifics, but it did tease that GTA 6' s morality system would be more complex than RDR2's "honor" system. In that iteration of the mechanic, Rockstar tended to reward playing as a "good" guy, but GTA 6 won't be as cut and dry. The magazine also claimed that the game would have "deep relationship mechanics" of some sort. Between these tidbits and the way GTA 6 keeps track of players' habits, players may want to think carefully about how they move through Leonida.

GTA 6 is a more serious game

Rockstar likes to poke fun at social trends, and some of that humor will still be in GTA 6 — just look at how NPCs behave in the game's infamous nudist town. At the same time, Rockstar doesn't want the game to feel like a parody of Floridian stereotypes. Players should expect fewer "one-off" jokes when it comes to things like in-game brands or shops. The aim is to reflect a "believable culture," not a crass, childish one.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is coming to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X on Nov. 19.

articles.title: The Utility App Flood Won’t Last
articles.subtitle: The App Store is evolving at a breakneck pace not seen since its earliest days. We saw the first glimmers of what was to come early in 2025, but it wasn’t until late last year that the tsunami of apps developed with the help of AI agents really took hold.
articles.author: MacStories
articles.content:
The App Store is evolving at a breakneck pace not seen since its earliest days. We saw the first glimmers of what was to come early in 2025, but it wasn’t until late last year that the tsunami of apps developed with the help of AI agents really took hold.

Since then, veteran developers are releasing new apps and updating existing ones faster than ever, and new developers are releasing their first apps in droves. Today, supply is dramatically up, demand is flat, and quality is seemingly simultaneously up and down, depending on where you look.

How these forces play out long-term is anyone’s guess, but it’s worth examining because, just as Federico’s link to Bryan Irace’s post about agentic coding tools foreshadowed the rise of tools like Codex and Claude Code, today’s trends are sparks that have the potential to become tomorrow’s App Store wildfires or simply fizzle out.

Utility apps are on the front lines of this change. The TechCrunch story I linked in April picked up on this trend:

Another interesting tidbit from Appfigures is that the Utilities app category moved up the top five chart.

If anything, the trend has accelerated in the months since.

It’s not surprising at all that utility apps have taken off. They’ve been a staple of new developers since long before agents came along. That’s because many are UI wrappers around command line tools. That isn’t a knock against the developers of those apps; most users don’t want to open Terminal to convert a video or audio file to another format using ffmpeg, for example. By building a great UI around command line tools, developers have made them far easier to use.

However, the relative simplicity and narrow scope of many utility apps have made them a natural fit for AI agents, too. That’s why the App Store (and my inbox) is deluged with Mac menu bar and single-screen iPhone and iPad utility apps.

On the one hand, the abundance of utilities has been great for users. More choice means you’re more likely to find the app that perfectly fits your needs.

On the other hand, though, I don’t think what’s happening in the category is sustainable and expect to see it dramatically shift again in the coming months. As we’ve seen from reporting by The New York Times, app supply is outstripping demand by orders of magnitude, which will drive down prices. That alone is likely to cause the utility app market to shrink. But there’s more to it than that.

Remember, the demand shifts that The New York Times reported, based on Sensor Tower numbers, are for the entire App Store, where download numbers have grown 2-3% this year and last. I expect utility downloads to actually shrink in the coming months – again, because of agents.

Utilities, especially simple ones, are exactly the sorts of apps that are becoming trivially easy for power users – the very users these utilities are made for – to create themselves. From frontier labs‘ model improvements to a growing number of app-building tools from those same labs and third parties, it’s never been easier to build a web or native app yourself.

And although I agree with people, like Nilay Patel, who say the notion that everyone will build their own software is overblown, the utility market is different. Your average person is not downloading apps to adjust the frame rate and file format of a video or downloading YouTube videos to watch later.

But those are exactly the sort of things that people who are using agents are doing with them, whether they’re having an agent do those things directly via a command line tool in an app like Codex or Claude Code or building an app to do the same thing. That’s going to put even more pressure on the category.

That said, I think there will always be a cohort of users who would rather pay for an app than build it themselves, so I’m not predicting the demise of utilities in general – just the end of today’s frothy market. I also think there remains a place for simple utilities that solve hard problems with clever solutions. Not every utility is a UI wrapper for a terminal command. Plenty of apps feature original solutions or thoughtful and unconventional remixes of disparate tools.

Utilities aren’t going away, but just like other App Store deluges, the trend will recede. It’s just that this time, it’s likely to flip faster than usual.

articles.title: Danganronpa 2×2 Switch 2 Pre-Orders Canceled After It’s Forced To Be A Game-Key Card For ‘Unavoidable Reasons’
articles.subtitle: Danganronpa 2×2, the upcoming remake and retooling of the 2012 murder mystery, is canceling pre-orders for physical Switch 2 versions as developer Spike Chunsoft says that it has to release the game on game-key cards now for “unavoidable reasons.” The...
articles.author: Kotaku
articles.content:
Danganronpa 2×2, the upcoming remake and retooling of the 2012 murder mystery, is canceling pre-orders for physical Switch 2 versions as developer Spike Chunsoft says that it has to release the game on game-key cards now for “unavoidable reasons.”

The company doesn’t get into what those reasons are, but whatever the case, if you’ve pre-ordered Danganronpa 2×2 ’s physical editions (including the Psycho Tropical Vacation Package special edition) through its online stores, you should be receiving an email from the company confirming the pre-order has been canceled and informing you that if you want the game-key card version, pre-orders are up for that.

Pre-orders through other retailers will not be canceled, but will contain a game-key copy of the game when they show up at your doorstep in 2027. The company says in a statement that the “decision was not taken lightly and follows careful consideration,” and it “does not have any additional details to share at this time. ”

Well, that’s ominous. Game-key cards have become a contentious topic for Switch 2 owners, as these cartridges don’t actually include the game on them, but merely act as a way of confirming a digital license so it can be downloaded and played on the system. Nintendo has started opting to go this route for some of its own games as well, with Pokémon Pokopia also using them. Despite the controversy, it sounds like people are sucking it up and buying them.

Danganronpa 2×2 was originally set to launch in 2026, but was delayed during Anime Expo in July. The game is a remake of the original 2012 game, but also includes a new “Slayhem” route that will include a “what if” story with new killers and victims in its murder mysteries.

Apple’s M6 chip brings one of the biggest architectural changes to the base M-series since Apple silicon arrived, combining a new 2nm manufacturing process with a redesigned 12-core CPU, a larger GPU, twice the Neural Engine compute, and faster unified memory. However, the improvements vary considerably depending on the workload, which makes the M5 vs. M6 comparison more interesting than simply choosing the newer chip.

Apple introduced the M6 on August 25, 2026, initially inside the new Mac mini. The M5 arrived in October 2025 and has since appeared across products including the MacBook Pro, MacBook Air, iPad Pro, and Apple Vision Pro.

The M6 moves from the 3nm process used for M5 to a newer 2nm process, allowing Apple to fit more transistors into a smaller area while improving performance and power efficiency. The newer process also moves to gate-all-around nanosheet transistor technology rather than the FinFET design used with M5.

M6 CPU performance gets a significant redesign

The CPU represents one of the most important M6 changes because Apple has moved away from the traditional two-tier arrangement of performance and efficiency cores.

M5 uses a 10-core CPU with four high-performance cores and six efficiency cores. M6 expands this to 12 cores consisting of two new “super cores,” four performance cores, and six efficiency cores. Apple designed the super cores for demanding single-threaded workloads, while the performance cores join them when applications need additional multi-core processing power.

Apple says M6 delivers up to 1.2x, or roughly 20 percent, faster multithreaded CPU performance than M5. This improvement should become noticeable during longer workloads such as compiling large software projects, processing images, indexing files, running development tools, and performing CPU-heavy creative tasks.

For browsing, office work, streaming, messaging, and lighter photo editing, the M5 already delivers more performance than most users regularly need, so an M6 machine will generally feel similar during everyday interaction.

M6 adds two more GPU cores

M5 introduced a 10-core GPU with a Neural Accelerator built into every GPU core, giving applications dedicated hardware for GPU-based AI processing. M6 keeps this architecture while increasing the GPU to 12 cores and updating several parts of the graphics pipeline.

Apple says M6 provides nearly 30 percent more peak GPU compute for AI compared with M5, while geometry processing rates increase by 50 percent. The chip also includes updated shader cores, Dynamic Caching, and hardware-accelerated ray tracing.

New Mac Studio 2026: At a glance

What’s new: The 2026 Mac Studio gains M5 Max and M5 Ultra chips, dramatically faster AI and graphics performance, faster SSD storage, increased memory bandwidth, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and enhanced professional connectivity.

Release date: Announced on August 25, 2026

Price: From $2,499/£2,499

Pre-orders: Pre-order now

On sale: Shipping starts on September 22, 2026 but the Mac Studio with 512GB of unified memory is coming in late October.

Apple has launched a new Mac Studio to replace the M4 Max and M3 Ultra model introduced 17 months ago, in March 2025. Externally, the 2026 Mac Studio retains what Apple calls its “signature compact design,” with the most significant upgrades taking place inside.

The previous generation was unusual because it mixed chip generations, pairing M4 Max with M3 Ultra. The 2026 models bring both tiers into the M5 family, with M5 Max and the new M5 Ultra. M5 Max offers an 18-core CPU and up to a 40-core GPU, while M5 Ultra scales to a 36-core CPU and 80-core GPU. Neural Accelerators are now built into every GPU core to boost AI performance.

Apple claims up to 1. 3x faster CPU performance, 1. 8x faster graphics and 4. 3x faster AI performance, depending on the configuration and workload. M5 Max also adds third-generation hardware-accelerated ray tracing, while M5 Ultra can play up to 33 streams of 8K ProRes 422 video simultaneously.

Elsewhere, PCIe Gen 6-based SSDs deliver up to twice the storage performance, while Apple’s N1 chip adds Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. USB-C genlock, support for up to eight displays, and Thunderbolt 5 clustering for distributed AI workloads are also new.

When is the new Mac Studio available?

The new Mac Studio with M5 Max and M5 Ultra was announced on August 25, 2026, but it won’t start shipping until September 22. Even then, not every configuration will be available: Apple says Mac Studio models configured with 512GB of unified memory won’t arrive until “late October.”

You can pre-order the new Mac Studio now, though, and if you want one we’d recommend ordering early. Ongoing chip and component shortages have constrained Mac availability, so some configurations may face constrained availability, particularly high-memory models.

In June 2026, Apple raised the starting price of the Mac Studio by $500, from $1,999 to $2,499. The M3 Ultra model saw an even steeper increase, rising $1,300 from its $3,999 launch price to $5,299. The hikes were part of broader increases across the Mac lineup, which Apple attributed to sharply higher component costs, particularly RAM.

articles.content:
MacPaw has announced a long-term strategic partnership with Liquid AI to co-develop an on-device AI technology stack built specifically for the Mac.

The collaboration will start with Eney, MacPaw’s AI assistant for macOS.

MacPaw is teaming up with Liquid AI to bring more on-device AI to the Mac

Liquid AI’s Liquid Foundation Models (LFMs) will be adapted for Mac-based assistance and combined with MacPaw’s own on-device technologies: Mnemos for memory and Elix for inference.

Eney already shifted to a local model last year, keeping reasoning, contextual search, skill execution, and conversation history on the device whenever possible.

The new partnership is intended to push that approach further. The two companies are jointly developing the underlying stack rather than MacPaw simply adding another third-party model.

Once the technology has been tested and implemented in Eney, MacPaw says it plans to bring it to more of its products. It also wants to make the shared AI stack available to Mac developers through Setapp.

That could let participating apps expose more of their capabilities and context to Eney. This would allow the assistant to understand what is inside an app. It could also provide more useful answers or take relevant actions.
